newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian car output fell 7.3 pct in 1996 - Anfia.
newsitem.headline: Italian car output fell 7.3 pct in 1996 - Anfia.

text.p: Italian car production totalled 1,317,995 units in 1996, down 7.3 percent on 1995, but steady exports helped limit the decline, Italian car manufacturers' association Anfia said in a statement.

Anfia said the drop in output last year was mainly due to a contraction of the domestic market and the wait for a start-up in production of major new models, as well as protectionist measures brought in by Brazil.
But production was seen picking up in 1997, Anfia said, benefiting from a boost to domestic demand by the government's new car incentive scheme linked to manufacturers' discounts.
Exports in 1996, totalling 639,528 units, were just 0.34 percent off 1995 levels which Anfia said was a "brilliant result" given that 1995 exports jumped 18.5 percent on 1994.

Anfia said the result was even more noteworthy as Italian producers did not have the Brazilian market outlet last year as the country, by introducing protectionist measures in the form of prohibitive duties, practically blocked exports which in Italy's case were above 84,000 units in 1995.
Excluding Brazil, Italian exports rose by 14.3 percent and represented 48.5 percent of total production in 1996 against 45.1 percent in 1995.
